gaps.explanation: Revenue detail is only the all-funds Budgetary Comparison Schedule - Cash Basis - Total Primary Government (trimmed p20, printed p48, unaudited). Its governmental rows (indices 0-9) sum to 373,451 and tie to the statement rows they name. The other governmental receipts are not printed separately there: they sit inside the all-funds 'Local Receipts: Other' 2,674,318 (index 10, tagged business-type), which also holds all utility receipts and the Electric Fund loan proceeds. The governmental funds statement (trimmed p8 General / Street and Alley / City Hall / Park, p9 Pool / Grants) prints these rows per fund column: Franchise 3,563; Occupation 4,092; Carline 363+9+12+20+23 = 427; Charges for Services 7,333 (Pool); Lease Fees/Rentals 7,321+200+10,265 = 17,786; Fees, Permits and Licenses 1,203; Interest 998; Donations 8,250+1,120 = 9,370; Insurance Proceeds 2,239+2,590+1,679 = 6,508; Other Revenues 15,339+1,242+3,731+1,699 = 22,011; total 73,291. Fix: add those 22 printed fund-column cells and remove index 10 (combined all-funds line; user rule 2026-10-27: combined all-funds schedule lines are replaced by the fund columns). Every part of index 10 is carried by printed lines added in this file: governmental 73,291 (here), utility revenues 1,136,045 (proprietary statement p16, business-type revenue entry), Electric Fund 'Loan proceeds' 1,480,000 (cash flow statement p18, business-type other financing entry); 73,291 + 1,136,045 + 1,480,000 = 2,689,336 vs 2,674,318 = cash-vs-accrual timing only (p18 cash receipts: customers 1,046,852, miscellaneous 6,821, interest 67,355). Governmental: 373,451 + 73,291 = 446,742 = statement.

gaps.explanation: Business-type spending detail is the budget schedule's per-fund cash-basis 'Disbursements and Transfers' totals (trimmed p21, printed p49, unaudited): Electric 782,399 (index 12), Trash 112,345 (13), Sewer 107,369 (14), Water 132,498 (15) = 1,134,611. They are built from the cash flow statement (trimmed p18): e.g. Electric 525,950 suppliers + 114,594 employees + 60,953 purchase of capital assets + 9,056 unamortized bond discounts + 31,865 bond issue costs + 33,868 interest paid + 6,113 transfers = 782,399 exactly; they include capital purchases, principal paid and transfers out, so the transfers out cannot be added beside them without counting them twice. The JSON business-type disbursements are the proprietary statement (trimmed p16) operating expenses 966,104 + Bond Issue Costs 31,865 + Interest Expense 69,187 = 1,067,156, printed per fund column. Fix: replace the four budget totals with the printed fund-column rows of p16 (Electric 734,176; Sewer 103,332; Water 124,339; Trash 105,309; total 1,067,156) and keep the budget money that the statement does not expense on printed fund-column lines of the cash flow statement p18: Purchase of capital assets Electric 60,953; Principal paid on capital debt Sewer 50,000, Water 35,000, Trash 21,717 (= 167,670); the Electric unamortized bond discount (9,056) and transfers go to other financing. Result: schedule 1,067,156 + 167,670 = 1,234,826 vs statement 1,067,156; the 167,670 above the statement is printed capital purchases and debt principal that the accrual statement capitalizes / records against the liability (different basis, not removable without dropping printed spending). Remaining budget-vs-cash-flow difference: Sewer and Water budget lines are each 1,200 above their p18 cash outflows (budget also 2,400 above in transfers in), timing/budget classification.

gaps.explanation: Detail's only transfers line is index 11, the budget schedule's all-funds 'Transfers' 45,914 (p20, unaudited), tagged governmental but covering governmental and utility funds. The governmental funds statement (trimmed p10, printed p23) prints Transfers In General Fund 6,001 and Street and Alley Fund 30,000 (City Hall, Park 0; Pool, Grants 0 on p11); the utility transfers in (Sewer 3,800, Water 3,713, p17) are added under business-type transfers_net. Replaced index 11 with the governmental fund-column lines (36,001). Remaining 36,001 - 4,800 = 31,201 is exactly the printed Adjustments column (31,201) on trimmed p11 that nets interfund transfers in the Total column (gross per fund vs net Total; different basis by rule). 45,914 is 2,400 more than all printed fund-column transfers in (36,001 + 7,513 = 43,514); the budget also carries 1,200 extra in each of the Sewer and Water disbursement lines (budget classification), not carried.
